chapter_name: The Adventure of the Three Garridebs (by Arthur Conan Doyle)
learning_objective: 🎯 Put on your detective hat! Analyze Sherlock Holmes' brilliant deductive reasoning as he unravels a clever scam designed around an unusual last name.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An American named John Garrideb visits Holmes with a strange story: an eccentric millionaire left a massive fortune to be split between THREE men with the rare last name 'Garrideb'. They need to find a third man to claim the money.

They locate an old collector, Nathan Garrideb, in London. John tells Nathan he must travel to another town to meet the 'third' Garrideb. However, Holmes instantly notices inconsistencies in John's story and realizes it's an elaborate lie.

Holmes deduces that 'John' is actually 'Killer' Evans, a criminal. The entire 'inheritance' story was a fake plot to get Nathan out of his apartment. Why? Because the apartment previously belonged to a counterfeiter, and a massive printing press for fake money is hidden under the floorboards!

fun_activity.title: 🔍 The Observation Test
fun_activity.instructions: Holmes solved the case because he noticed John's clothing and accent didn't match his story. Look at a friend for 10 seconds. Close your eyes. Can you name the exact color of their shoes, their shirt, and if they are wearing a watch? Detectives observe, they don't just see!

exam_tips: 📌 Pay attention to the friendship between Holmes and Watson. When Watson gets shot, Holmes shows rare, intense emotional distress, proving his deep affection for his friend.
📌 The classic 'Bait-and-Switch' plot: The entire inheritance mystery is a distraction from the real crime (counterfeiting money).
📌 Holmes identifies 'John' is lying because he claims to be a lawyer from Kansas, but uses British slang and wears clothes that don't fit his American backstory.
quick_recap: ⭐ A man claims a fortune awaits three men with the rare name 'Garrideb'.
⭐ Holmes deduces the story is a lie designed to get a man out of his house.
⭐ The house secretly contains a criminal's counterfeiting machine.
